title: A use case's own fields — software-analysis capability
description: The front matter of one use case, a file `UC-NNN-<slug>.md` in `use-case-model/use-cases/` under the analysis location, optionally in a folder per functional area, whose name may open with a number such as `010-` (software-analysis DEC-001 points 1 to 3): one actor's goal and how the system fulfils it. The body says when it starts, the main path in numbered steps, the variants lettered after the step they branch from, and when it is done; steps and variants are append-only, since journeys and evidence cite them. These are the use case's own fields: its friction block sits in the methodology's container beside them and is the core's (COR-050, COR-053 point 10). A use case anchors to its actor and to each other actor it involves, as artefact anchors, and to the code it exercises and the decisions it relies on: those it rests on and those that answer it. It anchors each architecture view that realises it too (DEC-001 points 4 and 11); the capability's check requires each actor anchor. It anchors each requirement it lists in `requirements`, and the check requires those anchors to match the list (DEC-002 point 7). Its optional `after` names each precondition's producers, and draws no anchor (DEC-001 point 1). Applied by `pkit software-analysis validate`; unknown fields are refused.

title.description: The use case's title — its goal in a few words. The body's heading repeats it after the id, `# UC-NNN — <title>`, and the capability's check requires the two to match, so a reader of the front matter alone sees the title the page shows. It may change; the id does not.

actor.description: The actor whose goal this is, by id: an actor of its analysis, or one of an analysis it builds on, named with that analysis (DEC-001 points 2 and 4).

other-actors.description: Each other actor who takes part in the use case, by id: an actor of the analysis, never the use case's own `actor`. The body's *Other actors* says what the use case must protect for each. The capability's check resolves each to an actor and requires it among the use case's artefact anchors, so a changed actor flags every use case it takes part in (DEC-001 point 4). An actor of an analysis it builds on is named with that analysis, such as `core:ACT-developer`, and the use case anchors the records behind it instead (DEC-001 point 2). Absent, or empty, where no other actor takes part.

requirements.description: Each requirement the use case must meet, by id: a requirement of the analysis, of any of the three kinds, never withdrawn while the use case is in force (software-analysis DEC-002 point 7). Each is an artefact anchor of the use case, and the capability's check requires the requirement anchors to match the list exactly, so a changed requirement flags every use case that lists it. What meets a requirement is computed from these lists, and the requirement stores none of it. Absent, or empty, where it lists none.

after.description: Each precondition's producers, one entry for each line of the body's *Preconditions*, in its order (software-analysis DEC-001 point 1). A producer is a use case in force of the analysis that makes the precondition true, and any one is enough. An entry lists use-case ids, the use case's own among them, and `environment` beside them, never alone. It names the producers its line opens with, such as `**From UC-059, or Environment:**`. It draws no anchor. A use case with no precondition writes none. Where RS-SAN-009 binds, the capability's check holds it to the analysis, the words and the areas' numbers.
